verdict: Sandisk revenue exploded 378% to $11.0B and net income hit $8.1B as AI data-center demand sent flash-memory prices and margins soaring — gross margin reached 85%.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: vs $2,308M a year ago; +23% vs last quarter

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: operating cash flow minus money spent on buildings and equipment

segments.name: Datacenter
segments.note: Memory for AI data centers — up 61% in just one quarter and now the growth engine, from only $269M a year ago.

segments.name: Edge
segments.note: Memory built into cars, industrial gear, PCs and other devices at the 'edge' — the largest end market this quarter.

segments.name: Consumer
segments.note: Memory cards and USB drives sold in shops — down 39% as the company prioritizes higher-value data-center and edge demand.

opex.name: R&D
opex.note: Developing new flash-memory products and controllers.

opex.name: SG&A
opex.note: Sales, marketing and head-office costs — remarkably lean next to $11.0B of revenue.

takeaways.title: Margins are extraordinary
takeaways.text: Gross margin was 85.0%, up from 29.8% a year ago. Scarce flash supply and long-term customer deals let Sandisk keep almost every sales dollar after production costs.

takeaways.title: Cash is pouring back to owners
takeaways.text: Sandisk spent $5.0B buying back about 3.2M shares in the quarter and announced an 8-for-1 stock split effective November 19, 2026.

takeaways.title: A paper gain flatters profit
takeaways.text: Net income includes a $513M mark-to-market gain on equity securities. Excluding it and stock pay, non-GAAP EPS was $49.51 versus the GAAP $52.60.

oneTimers: $513M gain on equity securities (mark-to-market) inside other income — excluded from Sandisk's non-GAAP results.
